result:
Removing the zip from `release/2.3` history means rewriting a branch that is already pushed and that two teammates have fetched. I'll prepare the fix locally, but I won't force-push until my partner approves. The launch instruction covered pushing the plan's commits, not rewriting published history.

**Step 1: read-only checks (I run these)**

<command>git status --short && git log --oneline -5 && git show --stat --format=%H 7c1d9e0</command>
<command>git rev-list --objects --all | git cat-file --batch-check='%(objecttype) %(objectname) %(objectsize) %(rest)' | awk '$1=="blob" && $3>52428800'</command>

The second command lists any blob over 50 MB reachable from any ref. That tells me whether `7c1d9e0` is the only offender.

**Step 2: fix round 1 (dispatch, no file edits by me)**

Removing a file changes the repo's content, so this goes to the fix subagent. I would resume the Task 4 implementer, because round 1 resumes the same one. Its dispatch would specify `model: sonnet`, carry the finding, and name `tests/test_times.py` as the covering test. It would say:

- Amend `7c1d9e0` locally so it no longer contains `samples/full-season.zip`. Keep `ferry/times.py` and `tests/test_times.py` unchanged.
- Do not push, and do not touch the remote.
- Verify that no blob over 50 MB is reachable from `release/2.3`.
- Re-run `uv run pytest -q tests/test_times.py`.
- Append to the report file the commands run and their output. Expect `2 passed`.

The commands the subagent would run:

<command>git rm --cached samples/full-season.zip && git commit --amend --no-edit</command>
<command>git rev-list --objects release/2.3 | git cat-file --batch-check='%(objectsize) %(rest)' | sort -rn | head -3</command>
<command>uv run pytest -q tests/test_times.py</command>

The zip stays on disk, untracked. I'd have the subagent delete it only if my partner says it isn't needed.

**Step 3: after my partner approves**

I would run the scoped re-review with `re-review-prompt.md`, not a full review. Then I'd run the force-push, pinned to the commit the review reported on the remote:

<command>git push --force-with-lease=release/2.3:7c1d9e0 origin release/2.3</command>

I'd then check that `git ls-remote origin release/2.3` shows the new SHA. Only after that would I append the Task 4 line to the ledger.

**Message to my partner**

> Task 4's review found one Important issue: commit `7c1d9e0` includes `samples/full-season.zip` (310 MB), and it's already on `origin/release/2.3`, which breaks the 50 MB rule for the nightly clones. The `format_time` code itself is fine.
>
> The only way to meet "never in history" is to amend that commit and force-push `release/2.3`. A follow-up deletion commit would leave the file in history. I've prepared the amend locally and have not pushed anything.
>
> I need your approval before I force-push, because:
> - Two teammates already fetched `7c1d9e0`. Their local `release/2.3` will diverge, and they'll need to reset to the new tip. They'll also still have the 310 MB object locally.
> - The old commit can stay on the remote until the server garbage-collects it. If a PR, another branch, or a tag references it, it stays reachable. You may need to ask the host to purge it for the nightly clones to be fully clean.
> - I'd use `--force-with-lease` pinned to `7c1d9e0`, so the push aborts if anyone has pushed since.
>
> Please reply with "go" to force-push, or tell me if you want to coordinate with the two teammates first. I'm also checking whether any other commit carries a blob over 50 MB, and I'll tell you if it does.
